text:
elaine: Heads up — SRE alert: p99 gen latency (hosted eu-west-1) creeping to 2.8s, SLO is 1.2s. Dashboard shows queue depth up and repeated `batcher.max_batch_reached` events. Anyone oncall?
samir: seeing same. request_queue_depth per-shard trending up for ~30m; throughput steady. suspect continuous-batching pressure: max_batch bound preventing preferred kernel sizes so tails blow up. :fire:
ops-bot: alert: gen_latency_p99 > 2.0s for 00:28:12; affected pools: hosted-eu-west-1-prod.
maria: logs show many small requests batching poorly then getting forced into max_batch. We also have backpressure admission kicks — a chunk of clients are getting 429s intermittently.
kev: posting recent log excerpt and batcher metrics:
```
[2026-02-21T14:12:03Z] batcher: enqueue req id=0x7f3 len=24 tokens
[2026-02-21T14:12:03Z] batcher: enqueue req id=0x8a1 len=120 tokens
[2026-02-21T14:12:04Z] batcher: max_batch reached=32 drop_policy=admit_delay
[2026-02-21T14:12:04Z] admission: throttle client=api-key-zzz status=429 queued=48
[2026-02-21T14:12:05Z] gpu-runtime: p99_latency=2.6s
```
ops-bot: metric links: https://grafana.redwood/prod/eu-west1/batcher, https://grafana.redwood/prod/eu-west1/queues (short).
elaine: hypothesis: sequence-length skew + lots of short requests (20-40 tokens) causes many small items to occupy slots but max_batch tuned for large sequence throughput. Runtime ends up filling to max_batch too often which increases scheduling jitter and p99.
samir: options: 1) reduce max_batch to 16 for hosted pool (fast mitigation), 2) enable priority coalescing for short requests, 3) dynamic max_batch based on queue depth + recent seq-length histogram.
maria: immediate: can we throttle noisy clients by tightening admission control per-api-key? That should drop SLO violations quickly but could impact few customers.
kev: cost/ops note: reducing max_batch will reduce throughput efficiency and increase GPU token cost — approx +12% unit cost in sims. Getting more capacity (spin up 2 more nodes) also helps but costs more.
elaine: I'm leaning to two-step: 1) tighten per-key admission for top 10 noisy keys (3-5m) + enable short-request coalescing flag on batcher (hotfix), 2) schedule dynamic max_batch work for next sprint. Who can push the hotfix?
samir: I can push the admission tweak and optional flag. Will need a quick config rollout to hosted-eu-west-1 and a canary.
maria: I'll compile the noisy-client list and notify account team. Also start a runbook entry for this pattern.
ops-bot: action created: TASK-3821 - reduce noisy-client concurrency + enable short-coalesce in eu-west-1. assignee=samir.
kev: one more thought — we saw similar tail regressions after the quantization kernel switch last month. Confirm kernel selection hasn't regressed for short sequences.
elaine: good call, kev. samir, can you validate kernel profiles in the canary logs? if kernels are suboptimal we fallback to older kernel build.
samir: will validate. deploying admission tweak to canary now (eu-west-1-a). ETA 8m.
elaine: thanks — please ping when canary green. I'll update slack channels and SRE incident doc. :eyes:
ops-bot: deployment status: canary started TASK-3821 at 1759001320 by samir.
samir: canary reported p99 down from 2.8s -> 1.1s in the canary shard after admission tighten + coalesce flag. rolling to remaining shards.
maria: nice. I'm drafting customer notif for the handful of affected API keys.
kev: keep an eye on cost dashboards — if we stay at tighter admission long-term we might need to re-evaluate reserved capacity.
elaine: agreed. postmortem checklist item: add telemetry to correlate max_batch hit rate with p99 latency, and add a safety rule to auto-reduce max_batch when queue depth crosses X and small-seq fraction > Y.
ops-bot: incident closed: mitigated by admission + short-coalesce; follow-ups: TASK-3822 (dynamic max_batch), TASK-3823 (telemetry + safety rule), TASK-3824 (kernel profile audit).
